name: Wrist and forearm stretch (for desk workers)
noEquipmentAlternative: Seated or standing wrist stretches with the other hand, no equipment
musclesPrimary: wrist and finger flexors (flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus, flexor digitorum)
wrist and finger extensors (extensor carpi radialis, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digitorum)

prescriptions.reps: 1 round before yoga or typing-heavy work
1 hold per hand per stretch plus glides
2 rounds before Downward Dog or push-ups
1 hold per hand per stretch plus reverse-prayer and glides

Weight-bearing wrist prep (palms on desk or wall, then hands and knees)

setupSteps: Seat. Sit near the front of a firm, non-wheeled chair, feet flat, knees about 90 degrees (est.), back tall. A standing version (arm out in front, no desk needed) works too.
Clothes and jewellery. Slide sleeves up to the elbow, take off watch, bangles and smart-band so the wrist can bend freely.
Starting position. Shoulders down away from the ears, elbows soft, forearms free of the desk (or resting on it for the prayer stretch).
Warm the hands first. Rub the palms together for 10 seconds, or run them under warm water (est.). Gentle heat before exercises is suggested in an AAOS carpal tunnel handout (seen as snippet).
Rule for the whole set. Stretch to a firm, comfortable pull, never to sharp pain, tingling or numbness (every source seen says this).
Camera. Phone on the desk at forearm height, about 0.6 to 1 m from the side, so the elbow, wrist and hand are in frame (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Extend the arm
steps.action: reach one arm straight in front at about chest height, elbow straight but not locked, palm facing up.
steps.feel: shoulder relaxed, nothing yet in the wrist.
steps.visualCheck: side view, arm level with the floor, elbow open.

steps.title: Bend the hand down
steps.action: point the fingers toward the floor so the wrist bends down.
steps.feel: a mild pull starts on the inner forearm.
steps.visualCheck: the hand hangs from the wrist, forearm stays level.

steps.title: Add a light pull
steps.action: use the other hand to draw the fingers gently toward your body.
steps.feel: a firm but comfortable stretch along the palm side of the forearm; no pinch in the wrist.
steps.breathing: breathe slowly and steadily, do not hold the breath.
steps.tempo: hold 15 to 30 seconds (chosen 20; Mayo-linked and Healthwise pages say 15 to 30).
steps.visualCheck: elbow still straight, shoulder not hiked.

steps.title: Release
steps.action: let go, shake the hand loose.
steps.visualCheck: wrist back in line with the forearm.

steps.title: Repeat 2 times per hand (chosen; sources range 2 to 4)
Extend the arm, palm down
steps.action: reach one arm forward, elbow straight, palm facing the floor.

steps.title: Curl the hand down
steps.action: make a loose fist and bend the wrist so the knuckles point toward the floor (fist version) or keep the fingers straight (fingers-straight version).
steps.feel: a pull starting on the back of the forearm.
steps.visualCheck: fist hangs below the forearm line.

steps.title: Add a light press
steps.action: with the other hand, gently press the back of the hand toward you.
steps.feel: a comfortable stretch on the outer forearm.
steps.visualCheck: elbow straight; no twisting of the shoulder.

steps.title: Release and repeat 2 times per hand
Prayer stretch
steps.action: press the palms together in front of the chest, fingers up, elbows out to the sides.
steps.feel: light stretch on the inner wrists and forearms.
steps.tempo: lower the hands slowly toward the waist until a mild pull, hold 15 to 30 seconds (chosen 20; one source says about 30 seconds).
steps.visualCheck: front view, palms touching along their full length; wrists in a neat V.

steps.title: Reverse-prayer stretch (seated, elbows on desk)
steps.action: rest the elbows on the desk, turn the hands so the backs of the hands touch with fingers pointing down, and press the backs of the hands lightly together.
steps.feel: stretch on the back of the forearms; stop if the wrists pinch.
steps.tempo: hold 10 to 20 seconds (est.; sources range 5 to 30 s).
steps.visualCheck: both hands at the same height, shoulders low.

steps.title: Release and shake the hands out for 5 seconds
Make loose fists or relax the hands, forearms resting on the desk edge or held in front, elbows near the body
Draw slow circles with the hand, moving only from the wrist, 5 to 10 circles one way, then the same the other way (est.; the yoga source says 10 each way)
steps.feel: smooth, easy movement; no grinding or pain.
steps.visualCheck: forearm stays still; only the hand moves.

steps.title: Open the hand wide, fingers spread as far as is comfortable, hold 3 seconds
Close to a soft fist with thumb outside or tucked, hold 3 seconds
Repeat 5 to 10 times per hand (est.). A pregnancy handout (Mater) suggests a gentle fist-opening exercise repeated 5 to 10 times, several times a day

steps.part: F. Gentle tendon and nerve glides (optional)
steps.title: Tendon glides (six-position style)
steps.action: from a straight hand, move slowly through: straight fingers, hook fist (fingertips bent at the top two joints), full fist, tabletop (bend at the knuckles only), straight fist; return to straight each time.
steps.feel: smooth movement, mild tightness at most.
steps.tempo: hold each position about 3 seconds, 4 to 10 repeats (NHS leaflets say 4 to 6 times, up to 4 times a day; another handout says 10 times).
steps.visualCheck: front view, each position distinct, fingers fully open between positions.

steps.part: F. Gentle tendon and nerve glides (optional)
steps.title: Median nerve glide (gentle sliding version)
steps.action: with the arm out to the side and the palm up, slowly open the fingers and thumb and bend the wrist back a little, then relax. Move in and out of the position, do not hold it at the end range.
steps.feel: a very mild stretch; no tingling or pins and needles.
steps.visualCheck: side or front view, shoulder relaxed, no neck tilt.

commonMistakes.title: Bouncing or yanking the hand
commonMistakes.text: Bouncing or yanking the hand. It strains the wrist tendons and the nerve. Fix: apply a slow, steady, light pull and hold.

commonMistakes.title: Stretching into tingling or numbness
commonMistakes.text: Stretching into tingling or numbness. Possible nerve irritation. Fix: ease off until the tingling stops; if it keeps coming back, see a clinician.

commonMistakes.title: Bending the elbow
commonMistakes.text: Bending the elbow. The stretch moves to the elbow and loses the forearm. Fix: keep the arm straight but with a soft elbow.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath or hiking the shoulders
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath or hiking the shoulders. Tension builds. Fix: breathe slowly and drop the shoulders.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling on the fingertips only
commonMistakes.text: Pulling on the fingertips only. The finger joints take the stress. Fix: use the whole hand to push or pull from the palm and base of the fingers.

commonMistakes.title: Too long or too forceful a hold
commonMistakes.text: Too long or too forceful a hold. Little extra gain, more risk. Fix: stay at a firm pull, 15 to 30 seconds; two or three rounds are enough.

commonMistakes.title: Forcing the reverse-prayer position
commonMistakes.text: Forcing the reverse-prayer position. It is hard on stiff or sore wrists. Fix: keep the elbows on the desk and use a smaller range, or use the single-wrist stretch instead.

commonMistakes.title: Stretching but never changing the desk setup
commonMistakes.text: Stretching but never changing the desk setup. The stretch cannot undo hours of bent wrists. Fix: keep the wrists straight on the keyboard and take micro-breaks (workplace ergonomics sources).

commonMistakes.title: Doing nerve glides hard as a cure for CTS
commonMistakes.text: Doing nerve glides hard as a cure for CTS. Reviews show limited evidence and traditional glides may strain the nerve. Fix: keep them gentle and clinician-guided.

safetyNotes: Pain, numbness and tingling: stop if the stretch causes pain, numbness or tingling. Sources say to ease off and stay in a firm but comfortable pull.

Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) or wrist pain: NHS pages describe CTS as tingling, numbness and pain in the thumb, index and middle fingers, often worse at night, with possible weak grip. They advise seeing a GP if symptoms are getting worse or not going away or if home care is not working, and say mild cases can improve with changing activities, exercises and a night splint. This stretch routine is for comfort, not a treatment for CTS.
Wrist and forearm stretches for stiff or sore wrists: use the smaller range, skip reverse-prayer, and avoid forcing the hand.
After wrist, hand or forearm surgery or a fracture: exercises must follow the surgeon or hand therapist; some protocols avoid certain wrist and finger combinations for the first weeks.

Pregnancy: hand swelling and CTS are common; a Mater hospital page lists splints, positioning and gentle pain-free fist-opening exercises, and advises a doctor, midwife or physiotherapist if symptoms persist.
Diabetes and thyroid: stiff hands (diabetes) and hand tingling that may link to hypothyroidism (thyroid) are possible and need a doctor if symptoms persist.

Stop immediately if you feel: sharp or burning pain in the wrist or forearm; tingling, numbness or loss of grip that does not settle; sudden swelling, redness or a deformed wrist; dizziness or chest pain.
Gym etiquette: use the stretching area or step aside from walkways; at the office, use a stable, non-rolling chair.

Hold time and reps: 5 s, 10 to 20 s, 15 to 30 s and about 30 s all appear. We chose 15 to 20 s, 2 rounds.
Frequency: every 30 to 60 min, hourly, 1 to 3 times a day. We chose every 1 to 2 hours in desk work, at least once or twice a day.
Nerve glides: reviews show limited evidence; one article suggests traditional glides may strain the nerve. We made them optional, gentle and clinician-guided.
Wrist range: no clinical norms were found. Our angle thresholds are estimates.
Official AYUSH or MDNIY step text for Manibandha chakra: Not found.
Wrist-stretch-specific MET and clinical wrist-angle norms: Not found.
